ten_pada_head_and_neighbor.scope: The main text supplies the clauses for both verbal entries; its variant apparatus is kept distinct.

marker_decision.earlier_tradition: Śvetavanavāsin invokes kit in general; Ujjvaladatta sees no fruit for the k marker. Jñānendra notes the independently prescribed ī already excludes guṇa.
marker_decision.new_editorial_witness: At ten-pāda 9.1 n. 2, the 1943 editor expressly rejects the general kit account because a relevant operation is lacking, then quotes Ujjvaladatta. This is a direct judgment about the available explanation. It does not supply an independent positive effect.
marker_decision.cross_source_variant: Kṣīrasvāmin’s XML at 823 cites kal for the Yama-word lexeme and al for the hair lexeme, under different source readings. The 1943 printed main text of the ten-pāda work has kan and an respectively. No equivalence of the literal numbers 99 and 9.1 is needed to compare the words. Kṣīrasvāmin does not explicitly name Yama in that entry.

nominal_heads.selected_gloss: hair; explanations as agent and instrument at 9.2

accounting: One complete paradigm per lexical head. Agent and instrument are alternate explanations of keśa, not separate inflectional positions. The previously known ploughman and Yama are not counted as additional paradigms.
